excerpt_original: 16th Shanghai Biennale reveals title, Henri Cartier-Bresson Foundation honors Wolfgang Tillmanns and Poklong Anading, A Ma De Jia launches inaugural fair in Taiwan, and more. THE EDITORS

blocks.text: FERRAN BARENBLIT . Courtesy the Power Station of Art, Shanghai.

The Shanghai Biennale has announced the title of its 16th edition, “LOUDER,” set to open at the Power Station of Art in November 2027. Helmed by Argentinian curator Ferran Barenblit, the exhibition will examine how music, fashion, and other forms of popular culture influence our sense of identity, belonging, and collective desires. While the presentation will highlight rock, punk, hip-hop, electronic music, and C-pop, Barenblit told Ocula that “it will not be a biennale about music,” but rather an exploration of sound as a mechanism that can shape, unsettle, or even reinforce social and cultural hierarchies. At a press conference on November 11, Barenblit said, “Politically, we live in a world of constant friction. . . . Popular culture can reveal changes in society before we’ve even found the language to describe them.”
WOLFGANG TILLMANS at the Henri Cartier-Bresson Foundation’s gala on November 9, 2026. Photo by and copyright Say Who / Michaël Huard. Courtesy the Henri Cartier-Bresson Foundation, Paris.
Henri Cartier-Bresson Foundation Honors Wolfgang Tillmans and Poklong Anading

On November 9, the Henri Cartier-Bresson Foundation named German photographer Wolfgang Tillmans as the recipient of its Henri Cartier-Bresson Lifetime Achievement Award, and Filipino artist Poklong Anading as a laureate of its 2026 Latitudes program. Tillmans, who is known for his everyday still lifes, experimental abstractions, and intimate snapshots of youth culture, was honored with the EUR 35,000 (USD 38,700) prize for his role in redefining the photographic medium. Anading is a Manila-born artist whose oeuvre spans photography, installation, sculpture, and video, often addressing sociopolitical and environmental concerns. As a Latitudes laureate, he will receive a grant to produce his new series of work exploring the cultural heritage of underwater diving in Batangas, to be exhibited at the Henri Cartier-Bresson Foundation in Paris, the International Center of Photography in New York, and in the Philippines. The award ceremony took place during the foundation’s annual gala, coinciding with the opening of the Paris Photo Week and a retrospective of works by Henri Cartier-Bresson exhibition at the Caumont-Centre d’Art in Aix-en-Provence.
Yokohama Triennale Reveals Title and Theme for 2027 Edition

The 2027 Yokohama Triennale, titled “Whalefall: News and Rumours from the Ocean Floor,” is slated to run from April 23 to September 12, 2027, at the Yokohama Museum of Art. Led by artistic directors Cosmin Costinaș and Inti Guerrero, the ninth exhibition will explore oceanic phenomena and systems of maritime communication through two creatures: the whale, whose sinking carcass nourishes deep-sea ecosystems for decades; and the oarfish, whose appearance is believed to foreshadow natural disasters in Japan. The theme further draws on Yokohama’s history as a port city, and will extend its focus on seafaring and biological networks to contemporary technologies, probing how information circulates and alters collective narratives. Moreover, the Tange Kenzō-designed Yokohama Museum of Art has commissioned an architectural intervention that will transform the institution into the body of a whale.
A Ma De Jia to Launch Inaugural Fair in Taiwan

A new boutique art fair, dubbed A Ma De Jia (阿嬤的家), is set to take place from December 11–20 in Xiluo, Yunlin County, Taiwan. Founded by Michelle Hsieh and led by curator André Chan under the theme “In-transit (渡),” the fair will depart from the conventional booth format, transforming nine historic buildings and local spaces along Yanping Old Street into exhibition venues. 16 galleries from Taiwan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, and beyond are participating in the event, including Antenna Space, Capsule Shanghai, Hanart TZ Gallery, Kiang Malingue, Rossi & Rossi, and Yiri Arts. Commenting on the decision to organize a fair in Xiluo, a historic agricultural township, Hsieh said in a press release: “I want to create an art fair that can genuinely benefit a place. . . . I hope that, through art, more people will rediscover the value of this land, and that the people who live here will take pride in the land that has nurtured them.” Alongside gallery presentations, the 10-day program will feature collector previews, artist and gallery exchanges, and local cultural activities.
